cells.tense: You are following the line of your practice to where it gets simple.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Take something you really do practise and follow its pattern until the next step becomes plain to you — one turn, no proof owed to anyone.
cells.core:
In your practice, a line can be followed all the way to its end, and what waits there is usually plainer than the road to it. Nothing about the thing is still hidden. That state is available through small repeated work, not only through a revelation, and it tends to arrive quietly between two ordinary sessions.

The invitation sitting on top is the reasoning that clears room rather than the reasoning that pins down. So take something you really do practise and follow its pattern until the next step becomes plain — one turn, no proof owed to anyone. Understanding like that loosens the pattern instead of locking it. What you end up with isn't a conclusion. It's a clearer place from which to take the next repetition.
cells.sheetLine: Follow the practice until the next step is plain.
cells.verb: seeing a thing through to where nothing about it is left hidden
cells.place: a small practice kept alive by regular attention, where skill is built by repetition

cells.tense: You are trying to hold the finished shape of the practice before the next repetition has started.
cells.act: light it and do not decide yet what it is for
cells.ask: Begin a small piece of practice this week with no purpose assigned to it. Finish it and let a day pass before you name what it was for.
cells.core:
In your practice, nothing is allowed to stay only half-seen. The whole picture is wanted before the next repetition begins, and that appetite now runs past the work itself. What comes first is the certainty that it will all be clear at the end. The middle, where skill is actually made, gets treated as delay.

What's thin here isn't effort. It's being new to your own practice again. So begin a small piece of it with no purpose assigned to it, finish, and let a day pass before you name what it was for. The freshness you're chasing is available at the start, before anything is proven. You can let the work be what it is without having already finished it.
cells.sheetLine: You want the finished shape before the first repetition.
cells.verb: seeing a thing through to where nothing about it is left hidden
cells.place: a small practice kept alive by regular attention, where skill is built by repetition

cells.tense: A practice has stopped and you are still keeping its hours on your calendar.
cells.act: define the seed of what will be built, in one line
cells.ask: Write a single line naming the practice you would actually build next, small enough to start tomorrow. Nothing else gets decided for now.
cells.core:
A practice of yours has stopped. The time is still blocked out, the equipment is still where you left it, and the thing itself is not happening. You keep standing at a door that is behind you, and the standing is what takes the hours.

The first resource is one clear direction held before anything is spent on it. So put the next practice into a single line: small enough to start tomorrow, specific enough that you could begin without deciding anything else. Nothing else gets decided for now. No old form needs arguing with or finishing. A new one named in your own hand takes the space the other one was using.
cells.sheetLine: The old practice stopped and you kept its hours.
cells.verb: seeing a thing through to where nothing about it is left hidden
cells.place: a small practice kept alive by regular attention, where skill is built by repetition

cells.tense: The regular practice gets kept, in hours you would say you did not choose.
cells.act: take the turning as it comes
cells.ask: Before your next session, sit still for a minute and notice one thing that is different since last time. Then start from there.
cells.core:
The regular practice is going. Someone is showing up to it and doing the plain hours, and according to you, it arranged itself. That isn't modesty. The thing is being made, and the maker has gone unnamed.

What helps here isn't more effort. It's letting each session be an arrival rather than a continuation. Before your next one, sit still for a minute and notice a single thing that has changed since last time, then start from there. Nothing has to be added to the practice. The one keeping it going can simply be recognized as the one keeping it going — because that is what's happening, and it can be signed.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it going and say it keeps itself.
cells.verb: seeing a thing through to where nothing about it is left hidden
cells.place: a small practice kept alive by regular attention, where skill is built by repetition

The sentence that serves me more than them would be 'you keep the small thing lit from underneath,' so it is gone from the core.
